props.title: Just Wright

sections.content: **Just Wright** (2010) fits into a unique niche of sports romantic comedies, following the path carved by films like **Love & Basketball** (2000). Queen Latifah brings authentic charm as Leslie Wright, a physical therapist who helps NBA star Scott McKnight (Common) recover from a career-threatening injury. The film refreshingly avoids many romantic comedy clichés by centering a professional, self-assured woman who isn't desperately seeking love or trying to change herself. It shares DNA with earlier basketball-themed romances like **Eddie** (1996), but grounds itself in more realistic NBA elements thanks to cameos from real players and authentic game footage. Love & Basketball|2000|A young woman pursues her basketball dreams while falling for the boy next door|Netflix Coach Carter|2005|Based on a true story of a high school basketball coach who benches his undefeated team due to poor academic performance|Paramount+ Eddie|1996|A passionate Knicks fan becomes the first female coach of an NBA team|Prime Video

The film stands out in the 2010s romantic landscape by featuring an African-American female lead who isn't relegated to sassy best friend status - a role Queen Latifah herself often played in films like **Last Holiday** (2006) and **Beauty Shop** (2005). The chemistry between Latifah and Common feels genuine, aided by both performers' musical backgrounds and natural screen presence. Their relationship develops organically through their shared love of jazz and basketball, rather than through contrived meet-cutes or misunderstandings typical of the genre.

While **Just Wright** follows some traditional romantic comedy beats, it elevates them through its sports rehabilitation storyline - a framework more commonly seen in dramatic films like **Creed** (2015) or **Million Dollar Baby** (2004). The physical therapy scenes add authenticity and raise the stakes beyond simple romantic entanglements, as both Leslie's professional reputation and Scott's career hang in the balance. Brown Sugar|2002|A music critic and record executive explore their lifelong connection through their love of hip-hop|HBO Max Creed|2015|The son of Apollo Creed trains under Rocky Balboa to become a boxing champion|Netflix Last Holiday|2006|A shy saleswoman lives life to the fullest after receiving a terminal diagnosis|Paramount+ SUBHEAD: Breaking Romance Movie Conventions

The film subverts typical romantic comedy tropes by having Leslie remain true to herself throughout. Unlike transformational narratives like **The Devil Wears Prada** (2006) or **Miss Congeniality** (2000), Leslie doesn't need a makeover or personality overhaul to find love. Her professional competence and authentic personality are portrayed as assets rather than flaws to be fixed. This approach aligns more with later films like **Hidden Figures** (2016), where female characters' expertise and intelligence drive the story.
